input: x = engine_rpm_state_t_0040b7ac.current_rpm (engine speed, 0.125 rpm per count); y = fuel_demand_computed (0x40a2ce, arbitrated fuel demand, 0.0679 mm3 per stroke per count)
output: local wVar3, the third (base value) argument of cm848_filterInputValue; its result injection_timing_aux_boost_blend is picked by max or min (DAT_00409094) against the three correction products into injection_timing_aux_output, and injection_timing_aux_offset = torque_limit_fault_snapshot - that output (when DAT_00409096 is 0, as in the RAM dump; otherwise -(DAT_0005a48a + output)) becomes the angle of the third (slot 12) TPU-A channel 6 injection event
units_check: x 4960..28000 = 620..3500 rpm; y 0..2061 = 0..140 mm3 per stroke (the 16 breakpoints are 0, 10, 20, 30, 40, 55 ... 140 mm3 at 14.72 counts per mm3); grid 0..143 = 0..16.8 deg at 0.1171875 deg per count (the offset is multiplied by -5 into an angle word that wraps at 0x7800 = 720 deg; the per-cylinder angle table steps by 5120 = 120 deg, so one angle count is 0.0234 deg and one timing count 0.1172 deg)
evidence: Of the five 19x16 rpm-by-fuel-demand maps this is the only one evaluated unconditionally; its result is the base value that cm848_filterInputValue blends the index-selected maps (L008-L011) against (result = base + blend_mode percent of the difference), so it is the default map of the auxiliary injection timing. The final value goes into injection_timing_aux_offset (main timing minus it) which engine_injectionAngle_tpuChannel6EventHandler multiplies by -5 into the angle of the third writeTpuEvent slot (cm848_calculateEngineFaultTiming only fires that event after the main injection); the 12 RAM words this function writes (0x40b830-0x40b852) sit at the same offsets as the e2m Aux_SOI_* outputs at 0x0180CE00-CE22, as outside corroboration.
naming_concern: The blend result is named injection_timing_aux_boost_blend although no boost is involved: boost_map_index_current / _target (0x40a4a6 / 0x40a4a8) are the lower / upper table numbers 1-4 of the blend (blend_weight spans 100 x index) and blend_mode is the percent weight of the indexed maps against this base map, so 'boost map' is a misnomer. torque_limit_fault_snapshot (the minuend) is the main injection timing written by cm848_calculateEngineTimingData, not a torque limit.

input: x = sensor_readings_t_0040baf2.coolant_temp (0x40baf4, 1/64 deg F per count); y = intake_manifold_temperature_sensor_filtered (0x40bb02, 1/64 deg F per count)
output: injection_timing_aux_coolant_factor (0x40b848); multiplied by the L003 result, divided by 4096 and clamped to +/-1024 into injection_timing_aux_combined_clamp, one of the four candidates picked by max or min into injection_timing_aux_output
units_check: x -2560..11520 = -40..180 deg F and y -2560..6400 = -40..100 deg F (round values at 1/64 F per count; flags 7 = signed x, y and grid); grid holds only 0 or 4096 = 0.0 or 1.0 in Q12: 1.0 when coolant <= 120 F and intake manifold temperature <= 60 F, falling linearly to 0 at 160 F / 80 F
evidence: Disassembly 0x527a3c-0x527a6c passes coolant_temp (r31 = 0x40baf4) and the intake manifold temperature (r26 = 0x40bb02) as x and y; the grid is only 0 or 4096 while the L003 grid is 0..145 and the two results are multiplied and divided by 4096 (helper 0x570f0), so this is the Q12 factor of the coolant (cold running) correction.
naming_concern: None for the destination injection_timing_aux_coolant_factor (only the abbreviation is spelled out); its product injection_timing_aux_combined_clamp is the coolant correction value, not a generic clamp.

input: x = engine_rpm_state_t_0040b7ac.current_rpm (0.125 rpm per count); y = fuel_demand_computed (0.0679 mm3 per stroke per count); no coolant input here - coolant enters only through the L002 factor it is multiplied with
output: injection_timing_aux_rpm_factor (0x40b84a); multiplied by the L002 factor, divided by 4096 and clamped to +/-1024 into injection_timing_aux_combined_clamp (the coolant correction candidate)
units_check: x 4400..22400 = 550..2800 rpm; y 0..1472 = 0..100 mm3 per stroke in 10 mm3 steps; grid 0..145 = 0..17.0 deg at 0.1171875 deg per count, nonzero (85..145) only at 600..1800 rpm and <= 40 mm3 (y <= 589), zero at 550 rpm, from 2000 rpm up and from 50 mm3 up
evidence: The L002 grid is 0 or 4096 and this grid is 0..145, and the two results are multiplied and divided by 4096 (helper 0x570f0) then clamped to +/-1024, so this table is the angle (the multiplicand) that the coolant factor scales; the product lands in injection_timing_aux_combined_clamp, which is one of the max / min candidates for the auxiliary injection timing.
naming_concern: The destination injection_timing_aux_rpm_factor is not a factor and not an rpm correction: the 0 / 4096 factor is the L002 coolant table, this one is an angle (0..17 deg) and rpm is only an input. Named by its role in the coolant correction instead; injection_timing_aux_combined_clamp is the coolant correction value.

input: x = intake_manifold_temperature_sensor_filtered (local wVar4, 1/64 deg F per count); y = sensor_readings_t_0040baf2.barometric_pressure (local wVar3, 0x40baf6, 1/18.56 kPa = 0.0159 inHg per count); 'ambient' here means intake manifold temperature x barometric pressure
output: local wVar3 (the factor); multiplied by the L005 result, divided by 4096 and clamped to +/-1024 into injection_timing_aux_load_limit (0x40b844), one of the max / min candidates
units_check: x -1280..6400 = -20..100 deg F (1/64 F per count; flags 5 = signed x and grid); y 1194..1697 = 19.0..27.0 inHg (round values at 0.0159 inHg per count; sea level is about 29.9 inHg); the grid is all 0 in this calibration, so the values check is vacuous and factor-versus-angle rests on the L002 / L003 pair
evidence: Disassembly 0x527b38-0x527b44 passes the intake manifold temperature (r27 from 0x40bb02) and the barometric pressure (r23 from 0x40baf6) as x and y, and the result is multiplied with the L005 result, divided by 4096 and clamped to +/-1024. The sensor-input table is taken as the factor and the rpm-by-fuel-demand table (L005) as the angle by symmetry with the coolant pair (L002 / L003), whose data confirm it; e2m lists the same split (Aux_SOI_Ambient_Corr temperature x pressure vs Aux_SOI_Ambient_Precorr speed x fueling).
naming_concern: The product is stored in injection_timing_aux_load_limit (comment 'load*rpm ... limit'), which is the ambient (barometric) correction, not a load limit.

input: x = engine_rpm_state_t_0040b7ac.current_rpm (0.125 rpm per count); y = fuel_demand_computed (0.0679 mm3 per stroke per count); no sensor input here - intake manifold temperature and barometric pressure enter only through the L004 factor it is multiplied with
output: local wVar4; multiplied by the L004 factor, divided by 4096 and clamped to +/-1024 into injection_timing_aux_load_limit (0x40b844)
units_check: x 4000..24000 = 500..3000 rpm; y 0..2944 = 0..200 mm3 per stroke in 20 mm3 steps; the grid is all 0 in this calibration (values check vacuous; the angle unit 0.1171875 deg per count is assumed from the shared +/-1024 clamp)
evidence: Same arguments as L003 but with its own axes (200 mm3 top instead of 100); its result is the second factor of the product (the first is the temperature-by-pressure table L004) that is divided by 4096, clamped to +/-1024 and stored in injection_timing_aux_load_limit, so it is the multiplicand (angle) of the ambient correction. Grids are zero, so the role comes from the structure, not from values.
naming_concern: The product's destination injection_timing_aux_load_limit is the ambient correction, not a load limit; 'ambient' stands for intake manifold temperature x barometric pressure.

input: x = engine_rpm_state_t_0040b7ac.current_rpm (0.125 rpm per count); y = cm848_calculateBoostPressure() (gauge boost: intake manifold pressure minus barometric pressure, 0.0159 inHg per count)
output: injection_timing_auxiliary_boost_factor (0x40b84e); multiplied by the L007 result, divided by 4096 and clamped to +/-1024 into injection_timing_auxiliary_boost_component (0x40b852), one of the max / min candidates
units_check: x 4800..24000 = 600..3000 rpm; y 0..6287 = 0..100.0 inHg of boost in 10 inHg steps (629 counts each at 0.0159 inHg per count); grid all 0 in this calibration (values check vacuous; flags 4 = signed grid)
evidence: y is the return value of cm848_calculateBoostPressure() (intake manifold minus barometric pressure) and the result is multiplied with the L007 result, divided by 4096 and clamped to +/-1024 into injection_timing_auxiliary_boost_component. The speed-by-boost table is taken as the factor and the speed-by-fuel-demand table (L007) as the angle by symmetry with the coolant pair (whose data confirm it); both grids are zero here.
naming_concern: None for this destination; the other half of the pair, injection_timing_auxiliary_fuel_demand_factor (L007), is the angle, not a factor.

input: x = engine_rpm_state_t_0040b7ac.current_rpm (0.125 rpm per count); y = fuel_demand_computed (0.0679 mm3 per stroke per count); no boost input here - boost enters only through the L006 factor it is multiplied with
output: injection_timing_auxiliary_fuel_demand_factor (0x40b850); multiplied by the L006 result, divided by 4096 and clamped to +/-1024 into injection_timing_auxiliary_boost_component (0x40b852)
units_check: x 4800..24000 = 600..3000 rpm; y 0..2944 = 0..200 mm3 per stroke in 20 mm3 steps; the grid is all 0 in this calibration (values check vacuous; the angle unit 0.1171875 deg per count is assumed from the shared +/-1024 clamp)
evidence: Same arguments as L003 / L005; its result is the second factor of the product with the speed-by-boost table L006 that is divided by 4096, clamped to +/-1024 and stored in injection_timing_auxiliary_boost_component, so it is the multiplicand (angle) of the boost correction. Grids are zero, so the role comes from the structure, not from values.
naming_concern: The destination injection_timing_auxiliary_fuel_demand_factor names the input (fuel demand) and calls the output a factor; it is the angle that the boost factor (L006, injection_timing_auxiliary_boost_factor) scales. Named by its role in the boost correction instead.

input: x = engine_rpm_state_t_0040b7ac.current_rpm (0.125 rpm per count); y = fuel_demand_computed (0.0679 mm3 per stroke per count)
output: wVar5 under boost_map_index_current == 1 and wVar6 under boost_map_index_target == 1 (two call sites, same tables) -> the first / second arguments of cm848_filterInputValue -> injection_timing_aux_boost_blend
units_check: same axes as L001: x 4960..28000 = 620..3500 rpm, y 0..2061 = 0..140 mm3 per stroke; grid 0..143 = 0..16.8 deg at 0.1171875 deg per count; it differs from the L001 base map in 81 of 304 cells, mainly nonzero values at 75..140 mm3 between 650 and 2200 rpm where L001 is 0
evidence: Selected when boost_map_index_current (or _target) is 1; cm848_filterInputValue interpolates between the maps of the two indices by blend_weight (compared with index x 100) and then scales the difference to the L001 base value by blend_mode percent, and the blend feeds the max / min selection of the auxiliary injection angle. Index 1 is the first of four ROM-adjacent 19x16 maps (e2m calls them Aux_SOI_Alpha1 / Chi2 / Chi3 / Chi4).
naming_concern: boost_map_index_current / _target (0x40a4a6 / 0x40a4a8) are not boost: they are the lower / upper table numbers 1-4 of the blend. The RAM dump (engine stopped) has both at 4 with blend_weight 400 and blend_mode 100, so map 4 is the map in use there.
